# The complete toolchain that compiles the backend dependency locks
# (src/backend/requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt).
#
# Installed by:
#   - .github/workflows/backend.yml, job "Lock staleness" (NFR-009 §2.3)
#   - `task deps:toolchain`, which `task deps:compile` and `task deps:check`
#     tell you to run first
# Both install THIS file, so CI and a local recompile cannot disagree about what
# produced a lock.
#
# Why the whole transitive closure and not just pip-tools
# -------------------------------------------------------
# pip-compile writes the invocation that produced a lock into the lock's header,
# and it reconstructs that line from CLICK's parameter metadata rather than from
# argv. A click minor bump therefore rewrites the header of a lock whose package
# versions and hashes are completely unchanged, and the staleness gate — which
# diffs the recompiled lock against the committed one — reports drift that no
# commit caused. That is what happened on 2026-08-27 (#1296): pip and pip-tools
# were pinned in the workflow, their transitive dependencies were not, click went
# 8.4.2 -> 8.5.0, and every backend pull request plus `develop` itself went red
# with the header comment as the only difference. Measured, not inferred: with
# pip-tools 7.6.1 held fixed, click 8.4.2 emits
#   `pip-compile --generate-hashes --no-strip-extras --output-file=… pyproject.toml`
# and click 8.5.0 emits the same line with `--no-index` inserted.
#
# `build`, `packaging`, `pyproject-hooks`, `setuptools` and `wheel` reach the
# output the same way — they parse pyproject.toml, normalise versions and build
# metadata — so they are pinned for the same reason, before rather than after
# one of them moves the locks.
#
# Deliberately WITHOUT --generate-hashes: Renovate's `pip_requirements` manager
# rewrites the version but cannot recompute a `--hash=` line, so a hashed file
# here would make every bot bump an uninstallable one. The pins are exact (`==`),
# and the job installs them with `--no-deps` followed by `pip check`, so an
# unpinned transitive that a future pip-tools introduces fails loudly and
# attributably instead of drifting into the output.
#
# Renovate keeps these current through the built-in `pip_requirements` manager
# (this path is outside the `src/backend/**` disable rule in renovate.json5) and
# groups them into one "python lock toolchain" pull request. That pull request
# may legitimately move the locks — header or content — so recompile them in the
# same pull request when `Lock staleness` says so; the gate running there at all
# is why `.github/pip-tools-requirements.txt` is in backend.yml's `paths:`.
#
# click carries an extra `allowedVersions: '<8.5'` cap in renovate.json5, scoped
# to THIS file: 8.5.0 is the release that broke the header, pip-tools 7.6.1 is
# the newest release and is affected, so there is nothing to bump to yet. The cap
# does not touch the click in src/backend/requirements.txt, which celery needs.

pip==26.1.2
pip-tools==7.6.1

# Transitive dependencies of pip-tools, pinned for the reasons above.
build==1.6.0
click==8.4.2
packaging==26.3
pyproject-hooks==1.2.0
setuptools==84.0.0
wheel==0.48.0
